doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Football instead of music in high school
summary: He was known as a football player until a broken ankle redirected his passion into music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did, just one more question about Olean, as a high school student did music give you an identity in the school? I mean some young men excel at being an athlete. I’m just wondering if you had this reputation as an outstanding musician?
That’s a good question because no, I had a reputation as being a football player.

I played varsity football as a freshman and I was captain of the football team as a junior. And I wanted to play with the Cleveland Browns, you understand? But I weighed 127 pounds and was 5’5” you understand? And I never got any bigger. I never got any bigger. But I loved — football was my life from the time I was about nine years old. And music was what came second. The only thing — right before the first game of my senior year some kid smaller than me jumped on me and broke my ankle. I never played my senior year. And so the passion that I put into football and sports transferred into the music. Even though I was always serious about music.
